findings.title: Advance unsupported vertical runs along the rendered axis
findings.message: Interaction layout advances X for every run, including unsupported vertical runs. The renderer advances Y for vertical runs instead. In a line containing vertical and horizontal runs, subsequent horizontal cells therefore receive a different origin from their rendered glyphs, misplacing selection fills and hit-test geometry.
findings.suggestion: Expose the run's advance vector or direction through the shaped-run interface and update the interaction offset along the same axis used by the renderer, even when the run contributes no interaction cells. Add a mixed vertical/horizontal run test.

findings.title: Make wrapped arrow transitions respect RTL paragraph direction
findings.message: Carets are flattened in top-to-bottom line order, with each line sorted left-to-right. Consequently, Right at the right edge of a wrapped RTL line jumps to the next line's left edge, and Left at its left edge jumps to the previous line's right edge. RTL paragraphs require the opposite cross-line transitions to continue visual navigation in paragraph reading order.
findings.suggestion: Preserve paragraph direction in the interaction geometry and handle cross-line transitions explicitly: for RTL paragraphs, Right crosses to the preceding physical line and Left to the following physical line. Test both transitions on a wrapped RTL paragraph.

findings.title: Choose the clicked line before comparing individual carets
findings.message: Vertical distance is evaluated for each caret rather than each physical line. With different font sizes or baseline offsets on one line, clicking above a short glyph can select a distant tall glyph because its vertical distance is zero, regardless of horizontal proximity.
findings.suggestion: First select a physical line using its aggregate vertical bounds, then choose the nearest horizontal caret among all carets on that line. Add a test with differently sized runs on the same line.
